[![CI](https://github.com/example/tinyqueue/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example/tinyqueue/actions) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/tinyqueue.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/tinyqueue) [![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tinyqueue/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/tinyqueue) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg) A tiny, lock-free, bounded MPMC queue for Rust. ## Features - **Lock-free** push and pop using atomics - **Bounded** capacity, decided at construction time - `no_std` support behind the `std` feature flag - Zero dependencies ## Installation ```toml [dependencies] tinyqueue = "0.4" ``` ## Usage ```rust use tinyqueue::Queue; let q = Queue::with_capacity(8); q.push(1).unwrap(); assert_eq!(q.pop(), Some(1)); ``` ### Benchmarks | Queue | push (ns) | pop (ns) | |-------|----------:|---------:| | tinyqueue | 12.1 | 11.8 | | crossbeam ArrayQueue | 13.4 | 12.9 | | std Mutex | 41.0 | 39.7 | Run them yourself with `cargo bench`. Results above are from an M3 Pro, see [the benchmark notes] (docs/bench.md). ## FAQ ### Is it really lock-free? Yes. Every operation is a bounded number of CAS loops. See the [design doc][design]. ### Why not just use crossbeam? You probably should! tinyqueue exists for `no_std` targets where crossbeam is too heavy. ## Contributing 1. Fork it 2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b feature/foo`) 3. Commit your changes (`git commit -am 'Add some foo'`) 4. Push to the branch (`git push origin feature/foo`) 5. Create a new Pull Request Please read CONTRIBUTING.md first. ## License Licensed under either of * Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) or http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) * MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) at your option. [design]: docs/design.md
